finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice record with no authentication and no ownership check (IDOR). The sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces an ownership check that this route lacks.
finding.source: invoices.py:7-8, route /invoice/<inv_id> with inv_id from the URL path (E1)
finding.sink: invoices.py:9-10, INVOICES.get(inv_id) then jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record (S1)

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> registered with no auth decorator
get_invoice(inv_id) takes the attacker-supplied path parameter
INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404); existence check only, no owner comparison
jsonify(inv) returns the whole record to the caller
Contrast: /my/invoice enforces inv['customer'] != g.user['id'] -> abort(404) on this same record shape

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, login_required decorator, or middleware anywhere in the repo (Grep for before_request|login_required|middleware returned nothing). No ownership comparison on the path. Only the 404 existence check applies. Caveat: if this route is meant to be admin-only, enforcement would have to be in an upstream gateway outside this repo, which I cannot verify.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the existence test `INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404)` at invoices.py:9, with no auth decorator on the route (invoices.py:7) and no before_request, login_required, or middleware anywhere in the repo. The sibling route's ownership check at invoices.py:16-17 is absent here.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches invoices.py:7-10: /invoice/<inv_id> has no auth or ownership check and returns the full record via jsonify(inv) at line 10, while /my/invoice/<inv_id> at lines 16-17 enforces the owner check. Any caller who can reach the route can read any invoice, so this is an IDOR; the one open point is that g.user is never set in this repo, so whether an anonymous caller can reach it depends on an upstream gateway I cannot see.
